Add packrat memoization so left-recursive expression rules work.

tool.cmd: cargo bench --bench parse_big && /usr/bin/time -l target/release/lexc big/2mb.lex 2>&1 | grep 'maximum resident'
tool.output:
parse_big/memo        time: [212.4 ms 214.0 ms 215.9 ms]
 parse_big/pratt       time: [96.3 ms 96.9 ms 97.6 ms]
   410238976  maximum resident set size

turns.assistant: Memoizing every rule on a 2 MB input doubles memory (180 MB with the Pratt parser vs 410 MB) and is 2.2 times slower. Left recursion is only needed for binary operators, which the Pratt loop already handles.

turns.user: Abandon packrat. Keep Pratt for operators.
LSP diagnostics are off by a few columns on lines with unicode. How do spans work here?

tool.output:
src/lexer.rs:3:pub struct Span { pub start: u32, pub end: u32 }
lsp/convert.rs:18:fn to_lsp_position(line_index: &LineIndex, off: u32) -> Position { /* utf16 */ }

turns.assistant: Spans are u32 byte offsets into the source, not char or column indexes, and files over 4 GiB are unsupported. The lexer never computes columns; LSP conversion goes through LineIndex and counts UTF-16 units. Any column displayed elsewhere must use the same helper.

turns.user: Good. Use LineIndex everywhere, never count chars in the lexer.
